{{Short description|Theorem in differential geometry}}

In [[mathematics]], '''Beez's theorem''', introduced by [[Richard Beez]] in 1875, implies that if ''n''&nbsp;>&nbsp;3 then in general an (''n''&nbsp;–&nbsp;1)-dimensional [[hypersurface]] [[Immersion (mathematics)|immersed]] in '''R'''<sup>''n''</sup> cannot be deformed.
